references.text: Earlier in the chapter, it is described how two onyx stones are to be engraved with the names of the sons of Israel, six names on each stone, as a memorial before the Lord.
Parallel text describing the actual making of the breastpiece with the twelve stones engraved with the names of the tribes.
The listing of Jacob's twelve sons who became the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel, whose names were to be engraved on the stones.
Jacob's blessing over his twelve sons, which form the twelve tribes of Israel represented on the breastpiece stones.
The listing of the twelve tribes of Israel with their leaders, showing the organization of the tribes.
The new Jerusalem has twelve gates with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve foundation stones with the names of the apostles, reflecting the symbolism of the breastpiece.
Moses set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel at the covenant ceremony at Sinai.
Twelve stones were taken from the Jordan as a memorial for the twelve tribes, showing similar symbolism with stones and tribes.
Complementary instruction in the same chapter detailing the engraving technique for the shoulder stones.
The initial command regarding the shoulder stones, which are part of the same representation system as the breastpiece stones.
A clear typological connection between the representation in earthly service and the completion of the heavenly city.
Describes the actual execution of the work on the onyx stones according to the command.
Complementary description of the function of the shoulder stones within the same representation system as the breastpiece stones.
